text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Vietnam's current law on foreign investment is too vague and open to various interpretations, Minister for Planning and Investment Do Quoc Sam told the National Assembly on Thursday. Sam was presenting the first revision of the country's foreign investment law since it was passed by the National Assembly in 1987.

-- The Executive Vice-President of the International Finance Corporation (IFC), Jannick Lindbaek, will visit Vietnam next week to consult with government and industry leaders on the World Bank affiliate's activities in the country.
-- Singapore has overtaken several Asian countries to become the second-largest foreign investor in Vietnam, and is well-positioned to take poll position after two investment projects are approved.
-- New telecoms conglomerate Global One is planning to introduce new services, including pre-paid calling cards and a U.S. Home Country Direct Service into Vietnam.
-- Former Politburo member Nguyen Ha Phan was dismissed as deputy chairman and deputy of Vietnam's National Assembly on Thursday.
-- Vietnam has set up a national commission for search and rescue on air and sea.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has launched guidelines for measures to prevent and solve the consequences of natural calamities in the Mekong Delta.
